ground_truth: In `getLatestComponentState` (component-tree.ts), the change wraps `metadata.dependencies = getDependenciesForDirective(...)` in `if (injector)`. Previously `dependencies` was always assigned on the directive metadata. Now `getInjectorFromElementNode` returns null whenever `ng.getInjector` is not supported (or returns nothing), and in that case `dependencies` is left `undefined`. The DevTools property view template evaluates `controller().directiveMetadata?.dependencies.length > 0`. The optional chain only guards `directiveMetadata`, not `dependencies`. So when an app's global `ng` lacks `getInjector`, selecting a component throws a TypeError reading `length` of undefined and the property panel breaks. The fix guards the template by first checking that `dependencies` exists before reading its `length`.
